name: Superlist
tagline: A polished task and list app that mixes checkboxes with freeform notes and real-time shared lists.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A personal task app with nested lists, markdown notes, keyboard shortcuts and local storage is genuinely a one-session build, and for solo use that covers most of what people actually do in Superlist. What does not survive the one-shot is everything around the edges: native macOS, iOS and Android clients, offline-first sync that resolves conflicts correctly, real-time shared lists with presence, and the integrations that pull GitHub issues, Slack messages and Gmail threads into a task. The animation and interaction polish is also a real part of the product rather than decoration, and agents do not reproduce that in one pass. If you work alone and live on one machine, the DIY version is fine. If you share lists with anyone or need it on a phone, you are signing up for a sync backend, which is the weekend that turns into a month.
coreLoopDIY: A local keyboard-driven app with nested lists, tasks, inline markdown notes, due dates, drag-to-reorder and JSON export, stored in the browser and running entirely on your machine.
requirements: A browser you are willing to keep a pinned tab in
Optional: a Tauri wrapper if you want a dock icon
whatYouLose: Real-time shared lists, comments and presence with other people
Native desktop and mobile apps with offline sync that actually reconciles
Integrations with Slack, Gmail, GitHub, Notion and calendar tools
The interaction polish and speed that make daily use pleasant instead of tolerable
Someone else's problem when your data disappears
moatNotes: Task apps are a commodity feature set with a non-commodity feel. The gap between a working list and one you keep using for a year is mostly craft.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the market for task apps is enormous and people churn out of the ones that feel slightly wrong. Superlist sells the sensation of a fast, quiet, well-behaved app across every device you own, plus shared lists that update instantly when your partner or teammate ticks something off. A self-built version wins on control and loses on exactly the axis that decides whether a productivity tool sticks: whether you reach for it without thinking. Add multi-device sync and it stops being a weekend project.
notes: Solo and single-device, build it. The moment a second human or a second device shows up, you are writing a sync engine, not a to-do list.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal task and list app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack (do not substitute):
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all persistence, no server
- dnd-kit for drag and drop
- Zustand for UI state only, data lives in Dexie

Data model:
- List: id, title, emoji, position, createdAt
- Task: id, listId, parentTaskId (nullable, one level of nesting only), title, notes (markdown string), done, dueDate (nullable), position, createdAt, completedAt

Features in scope:
- Sidebar of lists, click to open, inline rename, reorder by drag, delete with undo toast
- Task rows: checkbox, title editable in place, optional due date chip, expand to reveal a markdown notes editor per task
- One level of subtasks, indent with Tab and outdent with Shift+Tab while editing a title
- Enter creates the next task below and keeps focus, Backspace on an empty title deletes it and moves focus up
- Keyboard-first: Cmd+K command palette to jump to any list or search tasks by title, Cmd+Enter toggles done, arrow keys move between rows
- A "Today" smart view listing all tasks across lists with a due date of today or earlier, sorted by date
- Completed tasks collapse into a "Done" section per list, with a show/hide toggle
- Full JSON export and import from a settings panel, plus a one-click backup download

Explicitly out of scope: sharing, multi-user, real-time sync, mobile apps, notifications, integrations with Slack/Gmail/GitHub, AI features, any network request at all.

Quality bar: optimistic updates, no loading spinners for local reads, transitions under 150ms, works fully offline after first load.

Deliver: a README with setup and a single npm run dev command, seeded with two example lists on first run.
